source: npm pack @modelcontextprotocol/server-brave-search@0.6.2, tar xzf (not installed/run) in scratchpad adj-docs/modelcontextprotocol-server-brave-search-0.6.2/package/. The package ships only dist/index.js (274 lines, unminified). Paths below are relative to that package dir.

brave_web_search.rationale: The query only goes to the hard-coded Brave API host (api.search.brave.com), a fixed vendor endpoint, so this is not a SINK. The tool returns web search result titles, descriptions and URLs, which the threat model counts as attacker-controllable.
brave_web_search.evidence: dist/index.js:107-130 (fixed URL https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search, q=query; returns title/description/url of data.web.results); dist/index.js:225-235 (handler)

brave_local_search.rationale: Requests go only to fixed Brave API endpoints, so this is not a SINK. It returns third-party business listings (names, descriptions, hours) and falls back to web search results, which are attacker-influenceable.
brave_local_search.evidence: dist/index.js:132-161 (fixed api.search.brave.com web/search with result_filter=locations; fallback to performWebSearch at :152-154); dist/index.js:162-195 (fixed /res/v1/local/pois and /local/descriptions); dist/index.js:196-213 (formats poi.name, address, phone, descriptions); dist/index.js:236-245 (handler)

notes: Flags, toolset selection and read-only switches: none. Both tools are always listed (dist/index.js:215-217).

BRAVE_API_KEY is required. Without it the process exits at startup (dist/index.js:68-72), so no tools are served. It is not listed as a value condition because the variable can come from the inherited environment rather than the MCP config. It is sent only as the X-Subscription-Token header to the fixed Brave host.
No agent-supplied URL is ever fetched, and no file, database or local network access exists. The only outbound hosts are api.search.brave.com paths.
